priority.title: Scurceol Hyrde (Krondon): immune while his four orbs live
priority.evidence: docs/NIGHT-SIEGES-AND-MARFACH.md §1b: build 8d7baa3, 2026-11-05 14:27-15:40. 59-77 of 101 raiders fought him 3,219 units from his spawn; he stayed at 100%; all 42 raider deaths were to him; he was skipped every 20 minutes and switched back to; the Beran muster stalled at 2-5 of 50. 'Lyft' is in no log line. 2026-11-06 (168f55d): the tactic fired at 01:49 and 02:16, but every orb failed the ground-route gate and was set aside; the raid went to Fuladl.
priority.why: No damage is possible until the orbs die, and the raid never targets them: the orbs never attack, so the 'fighting the raid' switch never picks them, and melee can't reach them.
priority.plan: Fight him in his own room, not 3,000 units out where the raid met him, and kill the orbs from the floor below them first (the route shoots flyers from below), then everyone on him. Orb kills survive his resets. Built: required adds and fight at home (1.1.2). On the owner's PC (build e90bf21, 2026-11-11) the raid stood at four orb stands, one orb a party, and the orbs took no damage in 75 minutes; since 1.2 the whole raid's casters and archers take one orb at a time (tests only).

Period sources (Albion Encounters Guide, VN Boards, Feb 2003; Allakhazam comments 2003-2005; Herald, Apr 2002): aggro on the main tank because he heals by kills, kill the lesser monsters first, a ported group runs across Behemoth's chamber to the portal. The script differs from the period fight: it ends bladeturns and blasts after five (the guide used pulsing bladeturns), and a raider far from him does no damage (the period hearsay: he must be fought on his platform). Not played. 1.2 upstream port (tests only): its scripts' death overrides run in ProcessDeath instead of Die (OpenDAoC-Core 0b581e3fb), so a death's counters, flags and spawns happen once per death even when Die is called twice; no mechanic changed. 1.2 upstream port by hand (tests only; OpenDAoC-Core fca5900d7, 403d084dc, 66dbe4220): his brain's flags (adds removed, throw, blast) are per brain, the 19 add bands are one array cleared on a reset, and the head count for a band is counted when it spawns (bots and the flood guard kept). His throw no longer re-checks his aggro inside the target loop (da1990cea). No mechanic changed.

aiTactics.summary: Raid plan (1.2 Legion, tests only; part of the Darkness Falls raid AI since 1.2, tests only). His room first: the route kills the Chamberlain (level 79, 792 from his spawn), Inquisitor Famuel and Earl Amagin (about 2,150-2,200 off, in the corridor) before it pulls him (period: clear the room, then pull before a respawn; PC log e3b8238: the Chamberlain joined Midgard's kill and killed two raiders, and he and Famuel joined Hibernia's second try). Main tank: the raid's tanks taunt him back onto a tank and a tank under 35% hands him to a fresh one; his tank walks him back onto his lair when he is drawn more than 1,200 off his spawn. Tank healers: the six raid healers nearest his target heal it first under 85%. Ranged line: casters, archers and healers 1,200 from him on the raid's side. Graspering souls (one per four raiders within 2,000 at each 5% step, at most 16 a step): casters and archers kill them while melee stay on Legion; a wave of more than four takes one melee party per four souls more, never the tank's party. Close range: he takes no damage from attackers more than 1,400 from him, so a raider farther out steps in to 1,100. Kill heals (2.5% per raider he kills): healers near him heal anyone under half first, and a raider under 35% who is not his target steps out to 1,700 until healed. Bubbles: no bot casts a bladeturn within 2,500 of him while he fights (he ends his target's and blasts after five). His throw: 8-16 raiders below his top five go to Behemoth's hall every 40-65 s, bots too; a bot walks across the hall to the zone point and is recalled only when it can't. Behemoth is never fought.

dodens-gruva/arosthespiritmaster.notes: Hand check 1.2: not in the world. No mob row of the release world database uses this class (world-spawns.json), so no raid meets it; the Aros the Spiritmaster of Dodens Gruva is SpiritmasterAros, the Dodens raid's final. The fight is in GameEpicAros (40,000 health, tether 3,500) and ArosBrain/ArosState, read here as this class's. Besides the rules below: on every hit he takes, each raider within visibility range (players and bots, EncounterTargets; upstream OpenDAoC-Core picks real players only) has a 3% chance to become his debuff target, and in his fight he also rolls 3% a brain turn on a random raider outside melee range: 1 s after the announce he casts Negate Spirit on that raider (spirit resist down 45 for 45 s in a 1,500 radius; no recast delay, so a big raid has it almost all the time). The same 3% per raider picks a bomb target once per spawn (the target is never cleared): he turns, walks to within 250 of them and 5 s later casts Soul Annihilation at his current target. Resists(), 100 resists while a 'Summoned Guardian' is within 300, does nothing: no NPC has that name and ResistsTwo sets the same values right after it on every turn. Fork changes (not upstream): CC-immune while walking home, and hits then put no one on his aggro list; when he is not attacking, his own NPC aggro check puts any pet or bot (a controlled brain) within 500 on his aggro list without the stock check's line-of-sight, stealth and stablemaster-route tests for bots.

The guardian runs a copy of his brain (ArosBrain), which finds the guardian itself within 3,000, so the guardian never takes damage either; it dies only with Aros (his death kills every Guardian of Aros within 4,000).
extraRules.tactic: Not in the world (no raid meets it). To play it: one raider pulls the guardian more than 3,000 from Aros and keeps it there while the raid kills Aros; the guardian dies with him.

One a fight: a hit that takes him from 100% straight below 90% skips it, and the stages start again only when he is idle at full health.
extraRules.tactic: Not in the world. To play it: pull the guardian away from him (it shields him within 3,000 and cannot be hurt itself).

extraRules.summary: Health stages, each once, when a hit takes him into it: below 100% the guardian summon; below 90%, 80%, 70%, 60%, 40%, 30% and 10% Soul Annihilation 5 s after an announce (3 s cast, 1,100 spirit damage in 750 around his target at difficulty 100); below 50% and 20% the big Soul Annihilation 5 s after its announce (6 s cast, 1,350 spirit in 1,500). extraRules.tactic: Healers top the raid up before each tenth; spread out of 1,500 before 50% and 20% where the room allows.

Fomor City has no raid of its own (no path in on its navmesh), so this steers the gamebots that fight there.

extraRules.summary: Berserker stance: while he has foes, a stance comes 20-35 s after the pull or after the last stance ended. For 10-20 s he has Strength 850 (hits much harder), is slower (speed 200, his template's 250) and larger (size 75), then his template Strength, speed and size come back. A stance that falls due while he is dead, out of combat or without foes is skipped and the wait starts again on his next fight (1.2, True 1.65 port: before, such a stance left the flag set and no Suttung went berserk again until a server restart).
extraRules.tactic: Tanks use their defensive abilities and healers focus the tank during berserk; off-tanks ready to take over. He is slower in the stance, so a tank can step back while it lasts. Expect one every 30-55 s of a long fight.
